newsitem.title: FRANCE: ATHLETICS-FREDERICKS BEATS RISING STAR BOLDON.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-FREDERICKS BEATS RISING STAR BOLDON.

text.p: Veteran sprinter Frankie Fredericks proved he was still going strong by defeating rising star Ato Boldon of Trinidad in a high quality 100 metres on Monday.

The 29-year-old Namibian won comfortably in 10.09 seconds ahead of American Brian Lewis, second in 10.19, and Nigerian Davidson Ezinwa, third in 10.20, on a rainy night in the Paris suburb of Saint-Denis.
Boldon, 23, who clocked the sixth fastest time ever of 9.89 last month in Modesto, California, came a disappointing fourth ahead of Canadian Bruny Surin.
"I'm pleased with my race," said Fredericks. "In such weather conditions, the time doesn't matter much."
Asked what he thought of Sunday's $1.5-million showdown between Olympic champions Donovan Bailey and Michael Johnson in Toronto, Fredericks said he knew Bailey would win.
Bailey crossed the 150-metre finish line unchallenged in 14.99 seconds after Johnson pulled out lame with a leg injury.
"What happened didn't surprise me at all," said Fredericks, who came back from Atlanta with two silver medals after being beaten by Bailey in the 100 metres and Johnson in the 200 metres.
"Maybe someday somebody will ask me to take part in that sort of thing but for the moment, I don't have the credentials," he added, hinting that he thought there was plenty more to come for him.

World indoor champion Hicham El Guerrouj of Morroco, who had said before coming to Saint-Denis that he would go for Algerian Noureddine Morceli's 1,500 metres world record of three minutes 27.37 seconds, could only manage a relatively modest time of 3:31.76.

"The conditions were not ideal and the pace in the first 500 metres was too slow," said El Guerrouj, who clocked a world class time of 3:29.51 last Saturday in the Dutch city of Hengelo. "Never mind, I'll try again."
American Bryan Robson had earlier run the fastest men's 400 metres hurdles so far this year with a winning time of 48.24 seconds.
Compatriot Derrick Adkins, the world and Olympic champion, fell before the last hurdle but he was not hurt.

American world champion Kim Batten, wearing her trademark sunglasses despite the miserable weather, won the women's 400 metres hurdles race in 53.63 seconds ahead of arch rival Deon Hemmings of Jamaica, the Olympic champion, who was second in 54.02.

"I didn't feel particularly good but it wasn't a bad race," said Batten after clocking the best time this year. "It's only my fourth meeting this season and there are still quite a few things I must work on," she added.

There was disappointment for high jump world record holder Javier Sotomayor of Cuba, making his first major outing since a disappointing performance at last year's Olympics followed by injury problems.
Sotomayor could only clear 2.25 metres and ended up fifth in an event won by Frenchman Didier Detchenique with 2.31.
